correctness.rationale: The forcing condition plus symmetry of \(R_Q\) gives equality of modal successor rows across every compatibility edge and hence across every compatibility component. If \(R_M\) is an equivalence relation, row equality and reflexivity force every compatibility component to lie within one \(R_M\)-class. Thus each \(R_M\)-class is a union of compatibility components. Conversely, any set partition of the component set defines an equivalence relation constant on components and therefore satisfies forcing. The constructions are inverse, so for finite \(c\) the count is exactly the Bell number \(B_c\), and for \(c=1\) the unique relation is universal. The bundled exhaustive verifier for carriers through five worlds is consistent corroboration but is not needed for the arbitrary finite proof.

originality.rationale: Tokuo's full primary text explicitly proves Theorem 3.2: a relation satisfies the forcing condition iff its successor set is constant on every compatibility component. The same paper defines the equivalence-frame class \(E\), and Lemma 5.2 shows that for reflexive symmetric modal relations satisfying forcing one has \(R_Q\subseteq R_M\). Consequently every compatibility component lies inside one \(R_M\)-equivalence class. Thus choosing an allowed equivalence relation is exactly choosing an equivalence relation on the quotient set of compatibility components, i.e. a set partition, whose finite count is the Bell number. The proposed census is therefore covered by direct implication from the published structural theorem even though the paper does not print the Bell-number formula.
